To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quantum-chromodynamic potentials, when supplemented by the nonpertur-bative confining and annihilation potentials, are able to fully account for the ground-state mass and hyperfine splitting data of all the quarkonia, including the light quarkonia, and also to make reliable predictions for the unknown mass and hyperfine splittings in the bu-bar, bsbar, and bcbar spectra.

the quantum-chromodynamics potential model for light quarkonia can be extended to the heavy quarkonia and to other p quarks provided that the perturbation potential is augmented by the nonperturbation confining potential and a nonperturbation annihilation potential.

the observed ground-state splittings of light and heavy quarks are fully accounted for if the potential is supplemented by a nonperturbation annihilation potential that rapidly decreases with increase of the quark mass.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the quarkonium spectra and the hyperfine splittings.
the investigation of the ground-state hyperfine mass splittings of the light and heavy quarks in quarkonium systems.
the development and application of the potential model for quarkonia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed mass spectra for all quarkonia are in excellent agreement with our quantum-chromodynamic-potential model.
our model is successful in explaining the observed spectra of light and heavy quarks.
the quantum-chromodynamic model is able to account for the observed mass splittings of all the quarkonia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is the nonperturbativities in the quarkonium dynamics which are responsible for the observed quarkonium mass spectra.
it is possible, in principle, to describe the quarkonium spectra by using only the perturbative and nonperturbative quantum-chromatic potentials.
the observed mass spectra and the mass splittings of all quarkonium systems can be explained by the same potential model with a single set of parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nonperturbatively generated annihilation potential is crucial for a proper description of the quarkonium spectrum.
the hyperfine splitting of the ground states of quarkonia is a consequence of a nonperturbatively generated annihilation potential.
a unified treatment of light and heavy quarks is possible in quantum-chromodynamics.
